title: Add inline video player to Bible reader
summary: Discovered videos marked "Play Inline" now play in a small player beside the Bible text (above it on a phone held upright) instead of in a pop-up window, and the player stays open while you change chapters. **Heads up:** at this commit no video in Seed Bible's content list is marked to play inline yet, so every video still opens in a pop-up and the tests in "The inline video player" can't be reached. Mark those Blocked unless a video opens beside the text. The other sections check that the reader and Discover panel layouts, which this change rearranged, still work as before.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the **Open the preview build** button above, on a computer in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you have the newest version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser, so it can show an older version. Do a hard refresh once: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. A private/incognito window also gives you a clean start.

setup.title: Turn on discovered content
setup.body: Open **Settings** and make sure **Show discovered content** is switched on. You don't need to sign in for these tests.

setup.title: Go to a chapter with a video
setup.body: Open **Matthew 26**. Its Discover panel lists a video called **The Last Supper and Pentecost...HERE!** by Expedition Bible. The tests below use it.

sections.title: Videos that aren't marked to play inline
sections.intro: Every video at this commit is in this group, so this is what testers will actually see.

tests.title: A discovered video still opens in a pop-up window
tests.why: The click handler now checks whether a video should play inline before falling back to the pop-up. Videos not marked inline must behave exactly as before.
steps: On a computer with a wide window, open **Matthew 26**.
In the Discover panel beside the text, click **The Last Supper and Pentecost...HERE!**.
expected: A pop-up window opens with the video's title at the top and the video inside it.
No player appears beside the Bible text.
Closing the pop-up brings you back to Matthew 26 where you were.

tests.title: Bible Project videos still open in a pop-up window
steps: Open **Genesis 1**.
In the Discover panel, click a video by **Bible Project**.
expected: A pop-up window opens and the video plays in it, as before.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed
sections.intro: The reader's layout was rearranged to make room for the player. With no video playing, it should look and behave exactly as before.

tests.title: The Discover panel still sits beside the text on a wide screen
tests.why: The panel now lives inside a new wrapper that's meant to be invisible when no video plays.
steps: Make the browser window wide (full screen on a laptop or desktop).
Open **Matthew 26** and scroll down through the chapter.
expected: The Discover panel is beside the text, the same width as before, and stays in view while the chapter scrolls.
The text is not squeezed or pushed off screen, and there's no sideways scroll bar.

tests.title: Moving the Discover panel below the text still works
steps: With a wide window on **Matthew 26**, click the compass button **Discover content** in the toolbar.
Scroll to the end of the chapter.
Click **Discover content** again.
expected: After the first click, the panel moves below the chapter text and is no wider than the text.
After the second click, it moves back beside the text.

tests.title: The last verses aren't hidden behind the panel
tests.why: A spacing rule at the bottom of the chapter was rewritten to find the panel in its new wrapper.
steps: With a wide window on **Matthew 26**, scroll all the way to the end of the chapter.
expected: The last verse (verse 75) is fully readable, with some space under it, and nothing covers it.

tests.title: On a phone, swiping between chapters still works and keeps your place
tests.why: The phone layout's swipe area was wrapped in a new container.
tests.before: Use a phone, or make the browser window narrow (about the width of a phone) and reload.
steps: Open **Matthew 26** and scroll about halfway down.
Swipe left to go to the next chapter, then swipe right to come back.
Scroll down and back up, so the header at the top slides away and comes back.
expected: Swiping moves smoothly to Matthew 27 and back, showing the neighbouring chapter while you swipe.
The chapter title isn't hidden behind the header at the top.
The header slides away when you scroll down and comes back when you scroll up, as before.

tests.title: On a phone, the Discover panel still shows after the chapter
tests.before: Phone or narrow window, as in the previous test.
steps: Open **Matthew 26** and scroll to the end of the chapter.
Tap **The Last Supper and Pentecost...HERE!**.
expected: The Discover items appear below the last verse.
Tapping the video opens it in a pop-up window.

sections.title: The inline video player
sections.intro: These tests describe the new feature, taken from the pull request description. They need a video marked "Play Inline".

setup.title: Check whether any video plays inline
setup.body: At this commit, Seed Bible's content list has no video marked "Play Inline", so clicking a video opens a pop-up instead. If that's what you see, mark every test in this section **Blocked** with the note "no inline videos in this build". If the PR author tells you which video now plays inline, use that video and its chapter instead of Matthew 26.

tests.title: Clicking an inline video plays it beside the text
tests.why: The video list at this commit has no video marked "Play Inline", so this can't be reached in the preview yet.
steps: With a wide window, open the chapter with the inline video.
Click the video in the Discover panel.
expected: No pop-up opens. A player appears beside the text, above the Discover panel, showing the video's title and author with a close (X) button.
The video starts playing on its own (some browsers block sound or autoplay; if so, press play once).
The player and the Discover panel both stay in view while you scroll the chapter, and they don't overlap.

tests.title: The player stays open when you change chapters
tests.before: The inline video from the previous test is playing.
steps: Go to the next chapter, then to a different book.
expected: The player stays open and the video keeps playing while you move around.

tests.title: Closing the player
steps: Click the close (X) button on the player. Screen readers announce it as **Close video**.
expected: The player disappears and the Discover panel goes back to its usual place and size beside the text.

tests.title: With the Discover panel below the text, the player still goes beside it
steps: With a wide window, click **Discover content** in the toolbar so the panel moves below the text.
Click the inline video in the panel below the chapter.
expected: The player appears beside the text, and the Discover panel stays below the chapter.
The page doesn't become wider than the screen (no sideways scroll bar).

tests.title: On a phone held upright, the player sits above the text
tests.before: Use a phone held upright, or a narrow browser window.
steps: Open the chapter with the inline video, scroll to the Discover items and tap the video.
Scroll the chapter up and down.
expected: The player appears above the chapter text, clear of the header at the top.
The chapter scrolls on its own below the player, which stays put.
When the header slides away, the player moves up into that space.

tests.title: On a phone held sideways, the player sits beside the text
tests.before: The player from the previous test is open.
steps: Turn the phone sideways.
expected: The player moves beside the chapter text, taking up a bit under half the screen.
The chapter is still readable and scrolls normally.

tests.title: In a split view, the video plays only once
steps: With a wide window, open a second tab side by side with the first (split view).
Click the inline video in one of the two.
Click into the other side so it becomes the selected one.
expected: The player only ever shows on one side, the selected one, so you never hear the video twice.
tests.why: The PR says the player only shows in the selected tab of a split view. Whether it should move to the newly selected side is not stated, so note what you see.

notCovered: The new optional "Play Inline" column in the content spreadsheet, which is read by a developer script when the video list is updated. It's covered by automated tests.
Direct video files and links that aren't YouTube or Vimeo in the inline player: every video in the current list is a YouTube video.
